keywords.def: microwave radiation detected from all directions, left over from the early universe
an earlier theory that the universe has always existed in the same state

starter: Which part of the EM spectrum has longer wavelengths than light?

teach.heading: The CMB
bullets: Originally very high-energy radiation, stretched by expansion

teach.heading: Two theories
bullets: Big Bang explains both red-shift and the CMB
Steady State cannot explain the CMB

model.problem: Evaluate the evidence for the Big Bang theory (6 marks)
steps: Red-shift: galaxies moving away, so the universe is expanding
Further galaxies recede faster: consistent with expansion from a point
CMB: predicted leftover radiation, detected from all directions
Steady State can't explain the CMB
Conclusion: Big Bang is the best-supported model

misconception.wrong: 'Just a theory' means a guess
misconception.right: A scientific theory is supported by lots of evidence

check.q: Why does the CMB support the Big Bang but not Steady State?
options: Big Bang predicts leftover radiation from a hot early universe
It only comes from the Sun
check.why: The CMB is explained as radiation from the hot early universe, stretched by expansion.

practice: Two pieces of evidence for the Big Bang
independent: Core: Summarise the evidence for the Big Bang
Extend: Write a 6-mark evaluation of the two theories
Stretch: Explain why scientists still refine the Big Bang model (e.g. dark energy).
